title: Mask Possession Animator
description: A floating Venice mask hovers before a face-captured head. The user choreographs a possession sequence by keyframing the mask's approach, attachment, and influence over facial morph targets. An energy conservation system ensures total animation energy across all keyframes remains constant, requiring careful balancing when editing.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that loads both facecap.glb (a head with morph targets/blend shapes) and venice_mask.glb (a decorative mask). Place the face-cap head at center and the Venice mask floating 2 units in front, slightly rotated. Use a PerspectiveCamera at z=4 with OrbitControls. Add warm ambient light and a directional light casting soft shadows.

Implement a timeline UI bar at the bottom with 12 keyframe slots. The user clicks a slot to select it, then adjusts these coupled parameters via on-screen sliders: (1) mask distance from face (2-0 units), (2) mask opacity (0.3-1.0), (3) face morph target blend weight for 'mouthOpen' (0-1), (4) face morph target blend weight for 'browInnerUp' (0-1), (5) head rotation Y (-30 to 30 degrees). Each keyframe stores all five values.

Enforce an energy conservation law: the sum of all parameter magnitudes across ALL keyframes must equal a constant budget of 20.0. When the user increases any value in one keyframe, the system proportionally reduces the same parameter across other keyframes to maintain the total. Display the current energy budget usage as a colored bar.

Interaction steps: select keyframe slot, adjust mask distance, adjust opacity, adjust mouthOpen morph, adjust browInnerUp morph, adjust head rotation, observe energy redistribution, select a different keyframe and re-adjust, use an Undo button (Ctrl+Z) to revert last change, use Redo button (Ctrl+Y), press Play to interpolate between keyframes with smooth lerp animation showing the mask approaching and possessing the face, press Reset to clear all keyframes.

During playback, smoothly interpolate all five parameters between keyframes using THREE.MathUtils.lerp. The mask should visually merge with the face as distance approaches zero. Show the current keyframe index during playback. All keyframe data and undo/redo history stored in arrays.
